judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition turns on whether 31% of total square footage is rented and used 'to conduct customary operations', a percentage test whose application to a partly tenanted apartment complex can be argued.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines 'building' for the Vacancy Provisions only, and must be squared with the blanket, multi-building schedule in the Declarations where the insured owns nine locations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of six perils plus a flat 15% reduction; the 60-consecutive-day trigger is objective.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Vacancy definitions and with the Special Form's specified causes of loss; fire is not among the listed perils, so the 15% rule governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Actual cash value' is the pivot of the whole condition yet is not defined in this form, and the $2,500 repair rule and improvements formula add further complexity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 B supplies a Kansas definition of Actual Cash Value and the Replacement Cost Optional Coverage replaces actual cash value entirely, so three provisions govern valuation together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line layering statement with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Accurately describes the stacking of Common Policy, Commercial Property and Additional Conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The penalty turns on 'the value of Covered Property at the time of loss', a phrase that can be read as actual cash value or as replacement cost, and the four-step formula compounds the point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be reconciled with the Valuation condition, the Replacement Cost Optional Coverage (which changes the valuation basis), the Kansas Actual Cash Value definition, the blanket 100% coinsurance entry and the Increased Cost of Construction blanket formula.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sampled text is physically interleaved with the Agreed Value and Inflation Guard Optional Coverages, so the mortgageholder paragraphs run into unrelated formulae mid-sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 C.4 replaces paragraph b. for townhouse buildings, and the interleaved Inflation Guard text bears on the blanket Limit of Insurance used elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short flat statement that repair or replacement cost excludes ordinance-or-law increased cost; the phrase 'attributable to enforcement of any ordinance or law' is the kind of boundary parties fight over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely opposes the Increased Cost of Construction Additional Coverage (c042), which applies only where Replacement Cost applies and expressly says its amount is not subject to this limitation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deletes one paragraph and caps valuation by contract liability; mechanical and self-contained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on the Declarations showing both the Replacement Cost coverage and this Extension; no inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed definition of 'fungus' including mycotoxins and by-products; precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated identically in the Special Form G.1 and echoed in CG 21 67 C ('fungi'); the duplication is harmless.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'pollutants' definition ('any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant or contaminant') is famously broad and frequently litigated at its edges.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same definition recurs in the Business Income form and CGL Section V.15, so the instrument is at least internally consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Stock' is defined by enumeration and is not naturally contentious for an apartment risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in Property Not Covered and the Finished Stock definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Duplicate of the first-Named-Insured cancellation right; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c005; duplication of the conditions across two cover jackets is redundancy without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 10/30-day notice structure is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Replaced by IL 02 61 A for Kansas, which adds mandatory statements of reason and enumerated grounds; the unamended text remains in the jacket.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mailing rule with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the parallel jacket provision and with IL 02 61 B.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short sentences on the effective date of cancellation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches its duplicate at c008 and the Installment Payments condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'May be less than pro rata' leaves the short-rate figure unstated, but the operative rule is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c009; no competing refund provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single evidentiary sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicated elsewhere in identical terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Integration plus endorsement-only amendment; standard and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c011 and coexists with the many endorsements that in fact amend the forms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Audit right during the period and three years after; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicate of c012 with no variation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clean statement that the insurer has the right 'but are not obligated to' inspect, with a closed disclaimer list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It differs from the first-jacket version (c013), which omits that qualifier and adds a boiler/pressure vessel carve-out — two copies of the same condition that do not read alike.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Premium responsibility and return premium allocation; two definite limbs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicate of c014; consistent with Premium Audit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Anyone having proper temporary custody' is loose, but the rule is otherwise clear; the copy reads 'as our legal representative' where the other reads 'your'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Small textual divergence from the duplicate at c015 and parallel to CGL Section II.2.c-d.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Deeming non-payment as a wish to cancel, with an imprecise cross-reference to 'Policy Conditions'; this copy omits 'and time'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Must be squared with the Cancellation condition and IL 02 61's Kansas restrictions, and it differs slightly from its own duplicate at c016.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A layering sentence identifying which conditions apply; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Accurately maps onto the Loss Conditions and Additional Conditions in the coverage forms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Void in any case of fraud' is severe but standard wording with a familiar materiality test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: IL 01 60 (Kansas) replaces this condition with a narrower non-payment rule, so two inconsistent concealment provisions appear in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Beyond your direction or control' plus the location-specific breach rule; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 C.2 supersedes it for townhouse buildings only, an expressly limited overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single anti-stacking sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicate of c020; coexists with Other Insurance and the separate Business Income limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two-year suit limitation is on its face definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 A substitutes a five-year Kansas period, leaving two different limitation periods in the same policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mechanical 45-day liberalization rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicate of c022; only mild tension with the endorsement-only Changes condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence denying bailees the benefit of the insurance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coexists with coverage for personal property of others payable for the owner's account.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pro-rata and excess limbs with an express formula; 'covering on the same basis' is the only soft phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicate of c024, and consistent with Property Not Covered k. and the trailers extension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Rates in effect at issue, recomputation at renewal; mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicate of c029 and consistent with Premium Audit and the non-assessability clause only in a mild sense.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Commencement during the policy period and a closed three-item territory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits with the Period of Restoration rule that expiration does not cut short the restoration period; conventional pairing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This copy reads 'to or from whom we make payment' (the other reads 'to or for whom') and again uses the undefined term 'Covered Income'; 'must to nothing after loss' is a typographical corruption.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The undefined 'Covered Income' has no referent elsewhere in the policy, and the copy diverges from its twin at c026.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Dividend entitlement 'if declared'; contingent but clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addressed to State Automobile Mutual while the Declarations name the stock company as insurer — a mismatch running through these mutual conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific meeting time, date and address; nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same issuing-entity mismatch with the Declarations as the other mutual-company conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short non-assessability rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: In mild tension with the Calculation of Premium endorsement and audit premium provisions, which contemplate premium beyond that stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line pointer to Section F Definitions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Special Form's definitions are in fact printed as Section G, so the internal cross-reference is off by a letter.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Risks Of Direct Physical Loss' subject to exclusions and limitations is the classic all-risk trigger; broad but well understood.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends entirely on Sections B and C of the same form, which are present and consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The anti-concurrent causation lead-in ('regardless of any other cause or event that contributes concurrently or in any sequence') is a phrase courts regularly construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs the eight exclusions that follow and interacts with the ensuing 'but we will pay' fire carve-outs, which is a familiar structure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion of enforcement of 'any ordinance or law' regulating construction, use or repair is broad but expressly illustrated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Increased Cost of Construction Additional Coverage says it is not subject to this exclusion 'to the extent that such Exclusion would conflict', an express acknowledgment of tension that must be resolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four enumerated earth movement categories plus volcanic action, with soil conditions spelled out; detailed and closed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The ensuing fire and explosion carve-outs align with the anti-concurrent lead-in.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Seizure or destruction by governmental order, with a firefighting carve-out; specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Civil Authority Additional Coverage in the Business Income form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'However caused' nuclear exclusion with a fire carve-out; short and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps the Nuclear Energy Liability Exclusion endorsement, which applies to liability coverages only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Failure of power or other utility service... if the failure occurs away from the described premises' is clear, though 'away from' does some work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly defers to the Special Exclusion B.4.a.(1) for Business Income, which uses the different trigger 'outside of a covered building' — a divergence in the two tests.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated war categories with definitions; standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the CGL War exclusions as amended by CG 00 62; no property-side conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Flood, mudslide, sewer backup and subsurface water are enumerated with a resulting-fire carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with the Water Damage definition in G.2 and the Water Damage Coverage Extension; the boundaries are drawn expressly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes presence or activity of fungus with carve-outs; the terms are defined and the exceptions enumerated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly yields to the Limited Coverage For Fungus in Section E of the same form, an internal harmonisation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single clarifying sentence that the exclusions apply whether or not damage is widespread.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reinforces the anti-concurrent lead-in; no competing provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare lead-in phrase introducing the second tier of exclusions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Notably it lacks the anti-concurrent language of B.1., a deliberate structural difference rather than an inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Artificially generated electrical current with a resulting-fire carve-out; specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the collapse and specified-causes provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Delay, loss of use or loss of market' is terse and its edge against business income claims is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against the Business Income form, which pays for loss of use of the premises during the period of restoration — the Special Exclusions in B.4.a. mediate that relationship.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Smoke, vapor or gas from agricultural smudging or industrial operations; narrow and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Does not disturb the specified-causes-of-loss inclusion of smoke generally.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list ending in catch-alls such as 'any quality in property that causes it to damage or destroy itself', with a resulting-loss exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exception routes back to the 'specified causes of loss' definition, which is supplied in G.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Voluntary parting... if induced to do so by any fraudulent scheme, trick, device or false pretense' is compact and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements the dishonest-acts exclusion; no conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excludes collapse 'except as provided below in the Additional Coverage for Collapse'; the reference is explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section D of the same form supplies that Additional Coverage, so the cross-reference resolves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The pollutants discharge exclusion depends on the broad 'pollutants' definition, and the glass carve-out is oddly placed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with the Pollutant Clean Up And Removal Additional Coverage and the specified-causes carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Steam boiler explosion with defined carve-outs for furnace explosions; technical but precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Limitation C.1.a. covering the same equipment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Continuous or repeated seepage... over a period of 14 days or more' is a bright-line test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits alongside the Water Damage Coverage Extension and the fungus provisions consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Neglect of an insured to use all reasonable means to save and preserve property' is an elastic standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates in substance the insured's protective duty in the Duties In The Event Of Loss condition, which is compatible.
